The displayed cot^3(alpha) relation is necessary, not by itself sufficient for flexible strings: tensile forces must be nonnegative; q=Q formally gives negative tension. Original physical model needs editorial clarification.
Airplane B flies EAST by SOUTH 30°, not SOUTH by EAST 30°; v_A/B magnitude about 916.5 km/h.
The 0.926 km/s day/night difference is conditional on equatorial alignment of the rotational surface velocity with the Earth orbital velocity; verify fig. 1.24 before releasing.
Source scan explicitly specifies theta=30 degrees; numeric tension/normal force and critical acceleration now evaluated at this angle.
Drawing board from under object requires relative slip; threshold differs from only overcoming table friction.

Book explicitly prints 38×10^5 km for ground control distance; retained as source text despite likely order-of-magnitude anomaly. Orbital result uses lunar radius, mass and 200 km altitude, not Earth-control distance.
Solar-Earth L1 and L2 approximate distance; rotation-frame assumptions explicit.
Book labels bottom pressure; computed force from hydrostatic pressure times bottom area, assumptions documented.
Critical theta=0 point needs quartic stability rather than second derivative test alone.
Moment flux force is calculated; pressure boundary conditions not provided for full bend load.

Source textbook fuel consumption 1.29×10^3 kg/s verified. Companion solution PDF page53 prints h=172 km, but independent analytic integration and numerical quadrature yield approximately 203.6 km with the book's assumptions; unresolved difference explicitly flagged.
Companion PDF page54 gives centroid 0.061a ABOVE cube center, equivalent to derived 0.561a ABOVE bottom; source fig 3.38 confirms cylindrical bore touches lower face.
Maximum charge error is 24×10^-21 e, not 24×10^-21 C; gravity dominates even worst-case electrostatic force.
Proof applies to the planar disk closing the hemisphere, not the hemispherical curved surface.
Uranium nucleus charge 92e; non-relativistic uniformly charged sphere model.
Textbook energy standard is table 4.1 on V1 PDF physical page131.
Original end-of-chapter 4.8 is vertical spring effective potential; do not confuse with 'thought question 4.8' on PDF p150.
Textbook energy standard is table 4.1 on V1 PDF physical page131.
Lightning energy is qU for constant average discharge potential; capacitive complete discharge from initial U gives 1/2 qU: not fully disambiguated by source.
Companion PDF p214 displays U with incorrect 1/r^2 (force dimensions), but its printed -4.0e-17 J numerically matches 1/r. Independent derivation uses U∝1/r.
Companion PDF p215 prints 2.81e-15m using k e²/R; physically assembled uniformly charged thin shell U=(1/2)k e²/R yields 1.41e-15m. Both retained; unresolved interpretation convention.
Companion PDF p216 uses 235g/mol for 1kg uranium; 1.50e14 J. If U238 is assumed, 1.48e14J; isotope not specified in main exercise. Nuclear fragment is Pd (Z=46).
Companion PDF p216 displays gravitational U∝1/r_min², dimensionally a force; p217 numeric 2.57e-48 J supports correct U=-G m M/r_min. Correct derivation and original typo documented.
Original theta is full HOH bond angle 104.91 deg, not 52.46 deg single semi-angle, corroborated by companion p81.
Textbook and companion printed 71 nm although C60 molecular diameter physically near 0.71 nm. Textbook Ek=6.21e-21 J; companion p81 Ek=6.12e-21J; both are preserved in solution.
Companion p88 uses China 2004 electricity 7.3e18 energy units in numerical ratio ≈11, but printed text incorrectly marks kW; model uses joules.
Insulating belt E=sigma/(2 eps), as derived companion p224, NOT conductor E=sigma/eps.
Original specifies no water-drop mass; independent calculation assumes 0.05 g. Companion p226 assumes 1cm³ (1g) and displays inconsistent potential calculation; under audit.

Textbook V1 PDF p209 problem6.2(3): x=-A/2 moving negative; companion S PDF p95–96 problem6.2(3): x=+A/2 moving negative and phi=pi/3. Different problem statement, preserve textbook with phi=2pi/3 and flag source divergence.
V1 physical p209 figure6.21 gives t=2.2s upwards zero crossing; candidate originally misread as +2.5cm, corrected.
Source V1 p210 second part scans as '向x方向' (no sign legible); companion S p97 explicitly '向x负方向'. Conditional candidate solutions retain both directions, companion selects phi1=2pi/3.
Textbook V1 p210 and companion S p98 clearly ask at x=A/2 find potential energy; correct 0.20J, earlier mis-transcription as K/U extremum corrected in questions and solutions.

Companion S PDF p105 explicitly assumes n=1 and E=3hnu/2, classical amplitude 1.63e-11m. Earlier candidate erroneously used hnu/2 (9.43e-12m), corrected. Source terminology '基态n=1' still conceptually inconsistent with conventional oscillator ground indexing.
Companion S PDF p107 confirms source diagram frequency ratio fx:fy=3:2, giving fy=1.8e4Hz; still awaiting source-vector TikZ redraw and third-party academic verification.

Textbook V2 PDF physical p99 says OUTER cell membrane surface positive; companion S PDF p232 says INNER positive, contrary to textbook. Original source retained (outer positive, E points inward); electric field magnitude and voltage difference unchanged but polarity reverses.

Companion S PDF physical p235 claims 2uF capacitors U/4 and 12uF capacitor 3U/4, but same page later imposes 3U/4≤200 V, yielding correct total 267 V. In actual circuit 12uF receives U/4, parallel 2uF+2uF branch receives 3U/4. Candidate correct.
Fixed-Q metal slab insertion decreases energy, but fixed-U insertion increases capacitor field energy while battery supplies twice the difference.
Companion S physical p238 obtains 2.1×10^-3 N downward for coaxial capacitor, matching independent initial force.
Inhomogeneous dielectric; upper surface bound charge -3Q/4, bulk +3Q/4, lower surface zero; source page102.
Textbook V1 p248 does not specify propagation direction; both +x/-x are mathematically valid. Companion S PDF p112 confirms the two sign branches; initial candidate wrongly forced +x.
Textbook V1 p248 says person thrown UP 2m, not ground amplitude 2m. From ballistic height obtain v=sqrt(2gh), wave A≈0.997m; companion S p113 matches, initial erroneous 2m amplitude corrected.
At t=4.2s nearest crest x=-0.4m traveled left past origin t=4.0s, not 4.5s (next crest); companion S p114 confirms.

Companion S p115 incorrectly labels phase difference odd π constructive, gives odd distances including midpoint x=15m; true initial antiphase requires even 2nπ constructive; independent x=2,4,...28m, midpoint destructive.
Companion S p117 reads graph P–S delay approximately 5.1 minutes; revised source estimate Δt306s -> distance7344km, previously guessed 5.0min/7200km.

Actual textbook V1 p236 eq7.45 M=0.67 lg(E/J)-2.9: M=9.2 -> E=1.147e18J, ~249 megatons TNT. S p117 rounds E early to 1e18J and reports ~217. Initial candidate mistakenly used different empirical Gutenberg formula 3.98e18J.
Full wake opening is 10 degrees; companion S p119 confirms half-angle 5 degrees. Wave speed=(60/3.6)sin5deg≈1.453m/s. Earlier tentative half-opening 10deg gave incorrect 2.89m/s, now corrected.
Cosmological redshift not uniquely represented by SR radial Doppler speed; conditional SR v≈0.724c.
Textbook V2 p118 and companion S p246: iron pipe INNER diameter2.0cm, OUTER2.5cm. Earlier candidate wrongly transcribed inner1.5/outer2.0, recalculated water current3.09e-4A.

Companion S p248 magnitudes 0.16A,0.02A,0.14A match independently written branch currents; arrows and sources require diagram-level review.

Original textbook V1 PDF p284 first asks distance AS MEASURED BY SPACESHIP when Earth reflects, not Earth-frame initial distance; correct 9e9m (companion S p127). Second Earth-frame ship distance on receipt 2.7e10m. Initial candidate mis-transcribed frame, corrected.

Companion S p129 solves 1.2e8 s ship photon arrival, 3.6e8 s Earth receives report and 2.5e8 s Earth sees event (rounded c=3e8). Independently derived with more precision; source comparison completed.

Companion S p134 defines '资用能' as invariant CM TOTAL sqrt(s) and rounds proton mass to 1 GeV, producing 6.7 GeV; candidate uses physical proton 0.938272GeV giving 6.4935GeV. Excess after subtracting rest masses is separate non-source definition, must not replace source result.
Companion S p135 confirms BOTH protons boosted so gravitational force ∝E² and each energy ≈1e18 GeV (assuming E0≈1GeV), ~1e15 times 1e3GeV accelerator reference. Candidate more precise 9.38e17GeV.
Three source drawings fig17.38(a,b,c), current orientation as read; all need independent diagram redraw.
Companion S p254 explicitly distinguishes orthogonal compass deflection arctan(5/18)=15deg31min from maximum arcsin(5/18)=16deg8min; independent calculations match.

Companion S p255–256 derives axial plus transverse half-circle field vector with sign dependent on original coordinate convention, corroborating need for BOTH components. Candidate uses rotated parameter convention; source figure redraw pending.
Half-infinite solenoid mouth flux half/full symmetry; r=sqrt(2)r0 interpretation requires flux tube approximation and independent figure review.
Companion S p259 confirms N=wire_length/(2pi MINOR cross-section radius) and B≈11.6T. Large toroidal axis radius=2m appears only in Ampere circumference, not turn wire length.
Magnetic flux for radial-axial open surface =mu0 I l/(4pi); disk perpendicular to axis has zero magnetic flux; geometrical surface must be specified.
Initial tire absolute pressure assumed1atm, torus centerline radius from 28in outer diameter, pump transfers intake gas at ambient p,T; answer3.94atm dependent on model.
Perrin counted layers 7160,3360,1620,860 each 30µm apart; independent NA estimates 7.60,7.47,7.10e23 mol-1, preserve scatter; do not replace with modern constant.
Saturated steam with liquid remains at 1atm on isothermal compression to half volume, contrary to naive Boyle doubling.

Companion scan S physical PDF p153 explicitly gives original textbook fig9.18 V_m,c=9.55e-5 m^3/mol and p_c=7.23e6 Pa; independent a=0.198 Pa m^6/mol², b=3.18e-5 m³/mol. Earlier rough external illustrative value was replaced.
High momentum electron p=1e-16kg m/s, r=p/(eB), needs momentum rather than nonrel me v.
High energy proton total 21.01GeV vs kinetic20.07GeV. Must distinguish what source means by 'energy'.
Numeric Hall carrier density≈2.86e20m^-3; N/P conduction type sign requires exact signed potential side A vs A' from original fig18.24; keep pending.
Source fig18.28(a) loop partial magnetic area, must determine individual in-field wire segments and torque relative pivot. Candidate conditional, figures not redrawn.
Classical electron ring radius3.86e-13m >> electron experimental effective bound1e-18m; electron quantum spin not literal classical orbit.
Original V2 p160-161 quotes F=(mu0 I²/(2pi))ln((a+r)/r), a=1.2cm r=6.7cm, L5m m317g v4.2km/s; candidate I≈4.12MA and average input~2.94e9W @40%. Check original geometrical labeling because a<r.
Different instantaneous magnetic parts between two moving charges do not obey pairwise Newton 3; total mechanical+EM field momentum conserved.
Main textbook fig10.22 A(10L,2atm),B(20L,2atm),C(40L,1atm),D(20L,1atm). Candidate A→B→C→D signed work+2.809kJ conditional on arrow direction; diagram arrows require final review.
Main textbook fig10.24 initial cylinder total volume30L: nitrogen35g in20L at2atm plus10L vacuum. Free expansion to30L no work/no ΔU, then reversible adiabatic to50L: T≈317.9K,p≈66.1kPa,W≈1873J.

Source V1 PDF p372-373 explicitly gives p1=2.7atm, body mass70kg. Independent adiabatic gas work gross332321J; 75% useful push minus atmospheric back-work203726J yields exit kinetic45515J and speed36.06m/s. Companion S PDF p164 instead substitutes p1=2.6atm and m75kg and reports ~29m/s; source-parameter mismatch preserved, not silently reconciled.
Source formula gamma=(p1-p0)V0/[p0(V1-V0)] requires comparing equal-power heating experiments each starting from same initial state; not sequential isochoric then isobaric heating.
Gas work A>0 on expansion gives (p2V2-p1V1)/(1-n), but textbook may print denominator n-1 under external-work sign; candidate flags exact convention rather than blindly copying sign.
Three-reservoir reversible cycle includes extra intermediate reservoir heat: eta=T(T2-T1)/[T(T2-T1)+T1T2], not standard 2-reservoir Carnot.
Original four-state refrigerator table transcribed all p,V,U,liquid fractions, generated Qcold709.889kJ, Qhot933.396kJ, input223.506kJ, actual COP3.176 vs Carnot3.709.

Without regeneration, isochoric heat dumped to low bath and supplied from hot bath causes net cooling loss; candidate derives explicit COP correction. Figure10.32 requires external bath connection check.
Textbook fig19.25 companion S PDF283 reads H=220 A/m for B1.2T; original 6A with core, requires ≈26000A without core. Initial rough graph read 170 was corrected.
Companion S PDF284 reads H=170 A/m at B1.0T; 800 turns/m gives I=0.2125A. Initial rough graph read 150 was corrected.

Mutual L≈6.28µH, induced emf≈0.314mV for 50A/s. Flux per turn in b differs from total flux linkage by factor Nb100.
At fixed current as parallel pipes separate, magnetic force does positive work while B-field energy INCREASES. Source must supply twice the amount, A_e=A_m+ΔU_B=2A_m.

Source companion S PDF303 writes a numerical coherent-sum field not matching straightforward n*pi*(0.0026/2)^2*0.05 * E_single by about two decimal orders. Independent arithmetic gives upper bound E≈6.2e4 V/m, B≈2.1e-4 T (coherent hypothetical), NOT actual DC wire radiation. Need expert reconciliation.

Printed exercise uses positive I²R for energy entering rod; outward-normal Poynting surface integral must be -I²R.
At radiation/gravity balance net central force vanishes; initially orbiting particle travels tangentially if no other forces. Actual dust has optical efficiencies and PR drag.
Companion S PDF313 lists eastward sinθ=-5/8,-1/8,3/8,7/8; reverse initial-phase sign flips azimuth directions.
Minimum is m=1 nonzero grazing angle ≈5.74°, not m=0; assumes ideal mirror reflection phase π.
Source labels interval between two half-maximum positions as angular half-width; distinguish FWHM from single-sided HWHM.
Air-to-SiO2 and SiO2-to-Si reflections each have phase π, so relative phase is zero; at seventh dark k=6 and h≈1.277μm.
400nm is boundary of visible spectrum; solution uses 400–760nm convention.
485 and 679nm must be consecutive destructive orders; otherwise multiple integer solutions.
MgF2 1.38 is not sqrt(1.52), so quarter-wave coating reduces but doesn't strictly eliminate normal reflection.
Figure 22.37 is two-arm single-pass gas-cell setup: OPD=(n-1)d; do not insert Michelson double-pass factor.
Companion S321 gives unknown wavelength 5/7*600≈429nm using approximate single-slit secondary maxima; exact peak positions tanβ=β.
Original is single-slit harbor aperture; central width 2asin(20/50)=47.16°, not circular Rayleigh 1.22.
Image diameter ≈4.41μm; predicted illuminated receptor cells ≈2.29 with stated 1.5e5/mm² density.
Companion S322 uses satellite ground footprint including 1.5km launch-aperture width ≈7.19km; pure diffraction spread is ≈5.69km.
Original says centimeter wavelength band without a unique lambda; take 5cm only as explicit companion example.
Figure23.23 approx θ=41° for H-alpha 656.3nm second order and third-order spectral missing; d≈2.00μm, a≈0.667μm.

S325 says next principal grating order at ≈12.4°; local sidelobe peaks occur between 0 and 12.4°. First null ≈3.86 arcmin.
Davisson-Germer geometry surface in-plane adjacent atoms gives λ=d sin50°≈0.165nm, not naive bulk Bragg 2d sinθ.
Companion S329 uses effective projected polarization angle cosα=cosθ/sqrt(cos²θ+sin²θ cos²φ), not product of separate cosines.

Companion S330 uses n_e=1.4864, n_o=1.6584; e ray inside prism parallel base at r_e=30°, incident i≈48°.
Needs exact TikZ direction/polarization markings for pair of 45° calcite prisms, companion S330-331.
Original P1 and P2 are CROSSED, not parallel; independent Jones/Stokes yields I1=Ii/2, I2=Ii/2 elliptical, I3=3Ii/16 linear. Parallel-polarizer result 5Ii/16 would be wrong.
800nm quarter-wave retards 400nm by π, hence half-wave plate with orthogonally rotated linear polarization.
At glue interface ordinary ray i≈76.9° > asin(1.55/1.658)=69.2°, total internal reflection; extraordinary ray transmits.
Source S332 computes abs optical rotation≈49.9 degrees/mm, sign needs observation-direction convention.
At λ/8 relative phase π/2 circular, λ/4 linear orthogonal, 3λ/8 opposite circular, λ/2 initial linear; handedness depends viewer direction.
